journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains shown when tabbing out of the input, causing the Vanilla Calendar Pro to prevent the Tab key press to keep focus trapped within the calendar.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a focusout listener to the input that hides the datepicker when focus leaves the input unless it is moving to the calendar, ensuring the datepicker is hidden before the focus changes to the next field.

constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
    super(element, config)

    this._calendar = null
    this._isShown = false
    this._onFocusout = null

    this._initCalendar()
  }

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key will now move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field as expected.
functional_risks: Hiding the datepicker on focusout might interfere with users who navigate away from the input using means other than Tab (e.g., mouse click on another field) if the datepicker is still needed? But hiding on blur is common.
If the user clicks on the calendar, the focusout event on the input will fire, but we check if the relatedTarget is in the calendar and avoid hiding in that case.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that the datepicker is hidden when focus leaves the input unless moving to the calendar.
Verify that clicking on a date in the calendar does not hide the calendar prematurely.
Verify that the datepicker still functions correctly for mouse users.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker remains shown when tabbing out of the input, causing the Vanilla Calendar Pro to prevent the Tab key press to keep focus trapped within the calendar. The previous focusout listener hides the datepicker after focus leaves, but the keydown event is prevented before focus moves.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the input (capture phase) that hides the datepicker when Tab is pressed while the calendar is shown, allowing the default tab behavior to proceed. Also retain the focusout listener to hide the datepicker when focus leaves via other means.

  protected declare _onKeydown: ((event: KeyboardEvent) => void) | null

constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
    super(element, config)

    this._calendar = null
    this._isShown = false
    this._onFocusout = null
    this._onKeydown = null

    this._initCalendar()
  }

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key will now move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field as expected, while the datepicker is properly dismissed.
functional_risks: Hiding the datepicker on keydown might interfere with keyboard navigation within the calendar if the user tabs from within the calendar? But the listener only triggers when the target is the input, so calendar internal tabbing is unaffected.
The focusout listener might hide the datepicker when clicking on the calendar? It checks relatedTarget to avoid that.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that the datepicker is hidden when focus leaves the input unless moving to the calendar.
Verify that clicking on a date in the calendar does not hide the calendar prematurely.
Verify that the datepicker still functions correctly for mouse users.
